## Code-list mappings — How do we map ObServe code lists to ROS code lists and maintain these mappings? {#catalogue-correspondences-how-do-we-map-the-observe-catalogue-to-ros-and-maintain-these-correspondences}

Define correspondences between values in ObServe source code lists and ROS target code lists.

This topic concerns code-list values, such as species, countries, ports and gear types.

Define an initial mapping for French data and how other countries can reuse and enrich it for their own referential.

Agree how to handle new source entries and missing or ambiguous correspondences. These choices remain unresolved.

See the [initial LL correspondence inventory](ll-reference-correspondences.html) for evidence and open questions.

Set delivery levels after reviewing the inventory. Defer the R API design until implementation is considered.

### Shared mechanism

Use the [shared mapping design](../03-references/mapping-design.html) described under 03 — References.

This page defines concrete source fields, target code lists and correspondences for the ObServe-to-ROS export.

## Map ObServe code lists to ROS code lists

The ObServe foreign key identifies a source record. It is not itself the ROS code to write into the form.

For each mapped field:

1. Resolve the extracted technical ID using the ObServe catalogue's `topiaid` lookup.
2. Read the source attribute identified by the sheet mapping.
3. Match that value against the target ROS code-list lookup, including its existing aliases.
4. Write the canonical ROS value from the matched record.

The target code list comes from the ROS field binding. The source attribute comes from the sheet mapping.

Do not assume that every ObServe table's `code` column uses the ROS coding system.

| ObServe table    | Source attribute | ROS target table        |
| ---------------- | ---------------- | ----------------------- |
| `common.species` | `faoCode`        | `refs_biology.species`  |
| `common.country` | `iso3Code`       | `refs_admin.countries`  |

These are candidate correspondences to verify against the selected ROS fields and code-list values.

### Port conversion

Port conversion belongs to an export business rule, not the catalogue-mapping file.

The rule uses `common.harbour.locode` to determine a ROS port code.

The result is resolved through the existing `refs_admin.ports` lookup on `code`.
